incidents.sum: Opening a crafted message file makes Outlook connect to an attacker's server without its usual external-content warning, exposing the user's NTLMv2 login hash for cracking or relay. Microsoft rates it Moderate, but it was the one flaw already being exploited in a release of more than 1,000 fixes. The Preview Pane is not an attack route; the user has to open the file.
incidents.how: A crafted message file sent to the victim. Microsoft credits Benoit Sevens working with Anthropic's Claude, and a researcher known as nono. Attackers and victims have not been named and no indicators have been shared.
tl: Patched in the Office update. CISA adds it to its exploited list.
CISA deadline for US federal agencies.
incidents.fix: Fixed in Office LTSC 2021 build 16.0.14334.21048 and Office LTSC 2024 build 16.0.17932.21140. Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise users should confirm their channel has the update. Blocking outbound SMB and NTLM to the internet removes the leak path.

incidents.t: Outlook on the web: OWAReaper espionage
incidents.sum: A cross-site scripting flaw in Outlook Web Access on on-premises Exchange. The emails carried no link and no attachment. Reading one in OWA ran a hidden JavaScript loader that started the OWAReaper implant inside the browser, which collected mailbox details, settings and saved browser passwords.
incidents.how: Lures about supply chains, energy, tourism, public health and markets, sent from already compromised accounts. Proofpoint attributes it to TA488, a Russia-aligned group also tracked as Void Blizzard and Laundry Bear. Targets were government, telecoms, finance, hospitality and aerospace organisations in the US and Europe.
tl: Proofpoint publishes its report and names the implant.
incidents.fix: Microsoft issued emergency mitigations and then permanent Exchange updates. The implant changes mailbox folder permissions so access survives password resets: remove improper Default-user permissions, revoke EWS tokens, clear Outlook browser storage and block the known command servers.

incidents.sum: Three flaws chained into root-level code execution on fully patched VPN gateways, without a login. The actor, tracked as UTA0576, left no malware or web shell. It re-exploited the device for every command and edited logs, which let it slip past Ivanti's integrity checker.
tl: First exploitation seen by Defused. Volexity dates the chain to at least 3 Oct.
Ivanti discloses. Two of three flaws patched.
CISA lists the remaining two and requires forensic triage.
incidents.fix: Partly fixed on 13 Oct, with upgrade guidance for the full chain later. More than 5,500 gateways were exposed online.

incidents.sum: An internal messaging component did not check where messages came from, letting a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance. The China-linked group Armory Castle (UNC5221) planted the SAWFLY web shell and BARECLAW tunnel, harvested credentials, reached downstream systems and deleted logs.
tl: Exploited as a zero-day on one self-hosted appliance.
incidents.fix: Fixed. Self-hosted versions 24.3.1 to 26.2.3 need patch BT26-05-RS applied by hand. About six weeks passed between first use and the first patch.

incidents.t: Windows Shell Mark of the Web bypass
incidents.sum: A command injection flaw that strips the tag Windows puts on downloaded files, so a file opens with no warning, no read-only view and no macro block. It was the one exploited flaw in the largest Microsoft release on record.
incidents.fix: Fixed on 13 Oct. The third Windows Shell zero-day exploited in 2026.

incidents.sum: A path traversal flaw in the gateway's malware scanning. An emailed attachment writes files and runs commands as root on the appliance, and nobody has to open it. The second exploited flaw in this product in two months.
tl: Fixed builds ship as a hardening release.
Cisco confirms exploitation. CISA deadline 17 Oct.
incidents.fix: Fixed in 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780. Appliances that skipped the September release were exposed for a month.

incidents.sum: Two memory flaws in PHP itself that give unauthenticated code execution over HTTP. Details leaked the day before the fix. Chained with a Linux kernel flaw, they planted root web shells on 25 Palo Alto firewall management servers in under 15 minutes, with a suspected China link.
incidents.fix: Fixed for supported branches. PHP 8.1 and older got only minimal backports. More than 5.1 million hosts estimated exposed.

incidents.sum: An integer overflow reachable through a crafted regular expression in pipeline configuration, with no login needed on self-managed servers. Alpine Linux rebuilt its instance as a precaution.
incidents.fix: Fixed on 21 Oct.

incidents.sum: One crafted request to the remote-access SSL VPN makes the firewall reload, cutting remote access. It does not give entry. More than 51,000 devices were exposed.
incidents.fix: Fixed. No workaround exists.

incidents.sum: An out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decompression library, triggered by crafted compressed data. It reaches Node.js, Python Brotli packages, .NET, Bun, Envoy and Istio.
incidents.fix: Fixed in Node.js. Other runtimes patch on their own schedules.

incidents.sum: Four flaws chained into code execution on Plex Media Server. Not a zero-day: the fix shipped in August. Attacks began one day after details were published and installed crypto miners and proxies.
incidents.fix: Victims were unpatched servers.

incidents.sum: A memory flaw in Chrome's XML component, exploited in the wild. The eighth Chrome zero-day of 2026, matching all of 2025.
incidents.fix: Fixed. A browser relaunch is required.

incidents.t: VMware ESX logging gap and Linux kernel escalation
incidents.sum: The ESX flaw, scored only 2.7, lets an administrator-level intruder act without leaving log entries. The kernel flaw turns a PHP2Shell foothold into root.
incidents.fix: Vendor fixes available.

incidents.sum: Japan's largest furniture and homewares chain said up to 37.62 million customer records may be exposed, including names, contact details, birth dates and membership numbers. Passwords and card data were not exposed. The count is records, not confirmed unique people.
incidents.how: Not disclosed. The attacker had about three weeks of access before detection.
tl: Disclosed. Privacy commission and police informed.
incidents.fix: Access blocked and vulnerabilities fixed. Theft not confirmed. Customers to be notified.

incidents.sum: An automated campaign used 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to target 61,764 repositories. At least 1,835 repositories ran the injected payload and had their CI credentials stolen. Run logs were deleted, so the real count may be higher.
incidents.how: Stolen GitHub credentials opened probe pull requests, then injected a roughly 1,500-line payload into workflows.
tl: Campaign starts at 12:45 UTC, documented by Aikido.
incidents.fix: Ongoing. Owners of affected repositories should rotate every secret their workflows could read.

incidents.sum: Attackers stole billing information and datasets from AI model host Fireworks AI. Notion said chat transcripts from Notion AI customers using its Insights feature were taken, affecting about 1% of its customers. Fireworks believes the attackers wanted AI access tokens to resell.
incidents.how: The attacker breached Fireworks' cloud provider and used that to reach a Fireworks development system. Fireworks' second breach in two months.
tl: Notion cuts all connections to Fireworks and deletes stored data.
Uber confirms thousands of driver licence records stolen via Fireworks.
Uber notifying nearly 150,000 people whose data was taken via Fireworks AI.
incidents.fix: Notion disconnected. Fireworks confirmed customer data was stolen.

incidents.sum: A worm spread through cloud-hosted ScreenConnect remote management panels to at least 288 endpoints at 48 organisations within 90 minutes.
incidents.how: Huntress linked it to the RMM+ extension, which accepted a blank access key. Initial access has not been established.
incidents.fix: ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions as a precaution.

incidents.sum: Ransom notes appeared on campus machines and staff and students were told to shut down university devices. The gang claims more than 1 million Social Security numbers and full domain controller takeover. No samples have been published.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Active. The data claim is unverified.

incidents.t: Texas Health and Human Services claim
incidents.sum: A gang listed the commission and claims records on about 2 million Texans, including Medicaid, SNAP and banking data.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: The commission is investigating. No incident confirmed.

incidents.sum: A breach at newsletter vendor ARARA exposed 2,196,044 SEGA email addresses. Across about 380 client organisations, ARARA's systems were used to send about 7.13 million phishing emails.
incidents.how: Breach at the email vendor.
incidents.fix: SEGA says no names, addresses, card data or passwords were exposed.

incidents.sum: ESET disclosed a new toolset from the Russian group Turla running on compromised Microsoft Exchange servers at government organisations. It collected mail involving NATO and EU addresses.
incidents.how: Compromised Exchange servers. How they were compromised was not stated.
incidents.fix: Attribution is ESET's assessment.

incidents.sum: A bulk SMS provider left a database open with more than 125 million text messages from October 2022 to September 2026, including bank alerts and one-time login codes.
incidents.how: Database open to the internet with no login.
incidents.fix: Closed. Exposure confirmed, theft not confirmed.

incidents.sum: Government emergency alert apps sent millions of people fake chemical and nuclear alerts. Zelenskyy confirmed Ukraine had hacked back against Russia's app.
incidents.how: Compromise of the alert apps. Method not published.
incidents.fix: Not disclosed.

incidents.sum: Personal and medical data for 5.7 million patients was stolen, one of the largest healthcare breaches of the year.
incidents.how: Social engineering.
incidents.fix: Disclosed.

incidents.sum: The certificate authority disclosed that customer information and identity documents were stolen from a migration server left exposed since early 2025.
incidents.how: A migration server left open to the internet.
incidents.fix: Disclosed through an incident timeline.

incidents.sum: Unauthorised access to the carrier's online shop and My docomo portal exposed up to 294,839 accounts, including ID numbers and some bank details.
incidents.how: Under investigation.
incidents.fix: Services offline at last update. Customers warned to expect phishing.

incidents.sum: Maersk confirmed a breach of a legacy system inherited with its 2022 purchase of LF Logistics. The WhiteArmor group claims about 100 GB and demands $5m.
incidents.how: Entry through the legacy platform. Detail not published.
incidents.fix: Maersk says the incident is isolated with no effect on bookings. Data claims unconfirmed.

incidents.sum: Malicious builds of the open-source bee-js npm package and the Swarm Desktop app were published from two compromised GitHub accounts belonging to the Ethersphere project.
incidents.how: Two compromised GitHub accounts used to publish releases.
tl: Malicious npm package live for about 75 minutes; Swarm Desktop for about 8.5 hours.
incidents.fix: Package removed. The link to a known actor rests on shared infrastructure and is not confirmed.

incidents.sum: Two exploited flaws in Barracuda email appliances. One lets an attacker restore a crafted backup without logging in; the other runs commands as root.
incidents.how: Unauthenticated backup restore, then command injection through the timezone field.
tl: CISA adds both to its exploited list.
incidents.fix: Fixes available. Attackers and victims not named.

incidents.sum: A logged-in local user can become root on Check Point firewalls. Seen used after PHP2Shell access to plant a backdoor.
incidents.how: Local access, then escalation through the DynamicCLI socket.
tl: CISA adds it to its exploited list.
incidents.fix: Patch status not stated in reporting.

incidents.sum: An unauthenticated attacker can read files on the server through a flaw in the OCI-P service.
incidents.how: Crafted XML request (blind XXE).
tl: Added to CISA's exploited list. Deadline 24 Nov.
incidents.fix: Cisco fix available.

incidents.sum: A researcher published 33 alleged flaws in N-able's remote management platform used by IT service providers. Crypto miners were later found on 21 servers, 19 already on the latest hotfix.
incidents.how: Published flaws include authentication bypass and remote code execution.
tl: Hosted service taken offline, then restored.
incidents.fix: Hotfix 2 fixes 7 CVEs. On-premises customers told to take systems offline. N-able says it has seen no compromise.

incidents.sum: Attackers reached Maileva, which sends letters for hospitals, employers and landlords. Up to 22 million people's names and addresses are exposed, possibly with copies of letters.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Cybercrime unit investigating. La Poste says bank details were not taken.

incidents.sum: Expedia confirmed attackers reached its systems through a compromised data platform provider. The n0n group claims 830m+ loyalty records and 58m traveller profiles; unverified.
incidents.how: A stolen vendor key from Qubole gave a trusted path into Expedia's data platform, per Wiz and Sentra.
incidents.fix: Contained. Record counts unconfirmed.

incidents.t: TSMC employee data via cloud provider
incidents.sum: Employee data leaked through a third-party cloud provider. The attacker claims about 46,000 records.
incidents.how: Third-party cloud provider breached. TSMC says its own systems were not.
incidents.fix: Investigation ongoing.

incidents.sum: Australia's second-largest supermarket group disclosed a cyber incident and is containing its IT environment. No evidence of data theft so far.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Stores and online unaffected.

incidents.sum: A credential built into Wyndham's consumer app gave access to its member database, potentially millions of members.
incidents.how: Hardcoded credential in the app.
incidents.fix: Wyndham would not say whether it will notify members.

incidents.sum: About 820,000 members' numbers, emails and points balances exposed.
incidents.how: Unauthorised access; method not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Disclosed.

incidents.sum: North Korean hackers hijacked accounts to invite victims to video calls showing recordings or deepfakes of people they knew, then got them to install malware. More than $400m in crypto stolen.
incidents.how: Fake video call, staged technical problem, malware install.
tl: DOJ seizes the scheme's cloud infrastructure.
incidents.fix: Infrastructure seized. FBI issued guidance for victims.

incidents.sum: Attackers injected malicious JavaScript into websites using Optimizely's testing platform. 178 organisations were hit, 32 in finance, including HSBC, Equifax and ABN AMRO. The code was built to capture card details and tamper with crypto transactions.
incidents.how: A weakness in Optimizely's account signup, then script injection.
tl: Report URI findings reported by Reuters.
Optimizely update: a signup-flow flaw let the attacker impersonate users and inject JavaScript. BBC, CNN and Zoom among affected sites; payloads targeted crypto, card data and iPhones.
incidents.fix: Optimizely removed the code and reset access. Whether card data was taken is not confirmed.

incidents.t: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan: data via a service provider
incidents.sum: The n0n group leaked data it says came from Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase customers. Visa says the incident began at a third-party provider in Asia-Pacific and that card numbers and its own systems were not affected. Mastercard says a limited amount of information was exposed for a subset of cardholders in one benefit programme. JPMorgan says the data may include names and emails from marketing records held by third parties.
incidents.how: Through an unnamed provider.
tl: Data leaked. Mastercard confirms limited exposure; JPMorgan points to third parties.
incidents.fix: Card networks unaffected, per all three. The provider or providers have not been named. JPMorgan says its 16 Nov outage was a separate software bug.

incidents.sum: About 444,000 records exposed: policy numbers, names, phones, emails and portal IDs.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Services temporarily suspended.

incidents.sum: About 227,216 corporate and sole-proprietor email addresses exposed through the breach at email vendor ARARA.
incidents.how: Breach at the email distribution provider.
incidents.fix: Disclosed.

incidents.sum: Attackers reached the crypto card provider's card system. Card numbers, home addresses, phones and linked wallet addresses were exposed.
incidents.how: Access to the card backend; method not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Number affected not disclosed.

incidents.sum: Attackers sent transfers from the French cooperative bank's own account to exchange accounts opened under fake identities, converted the money to USDC and USDT stablecoins and laundered it across chains. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT put the loss at up to €118 million ($133m); the bank confirmed only the order of magnitude. Customer accounts were not touched.
incidents.how: Through a service provider's platform with access to the bank's network. The bank ruled out its online subsidiary Fortuneo and human error, and called it a sophisticated external attack. The provider and the exact access path have not been named.
tl: Withdrawals from OKX start at 12:25 UTC and run for about 21 hours across several exchanges.
ZachXBT reports a suspected theft from an EU entity.
Arkéa confirms the attack and suspends some transfers.
Crédit Mutuel's national confederation says part of the money was recovered.
incidents.fix: Bank says the incident is closed and under control and operations are returning to normal. Police and judicial investigation open. Funds partly blocked and partly recovered; the amount recovered has not been given.

incidents.sum: One attack campaign reached Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Hana and BNK Busan banks, the Yegaram, Welcome, DB and OK savings banks, Hyundai Capital, KDB Capital and several fintech and crypto firms. About 100,000 records were taken: names, contact details, incomes, loan limits and some resident registration numbers.
incidents.how: Externally reachable systems were probed and exploited, likely with automated, AI-driven tooling. A linked server carried a Chinese-language title for an AI autonomous penetration-testing console, possibly ARTEX. Authorities have not confirmed the tool or named an actor.
tl: First disclosures. Financial Services Commission holds emergency meetings.
incidents.fix: Investigations ongoing. Regulators ordered inspections of customer-facing and internal systems. Reported scale per firm: Shinhan ~25,000 customers, KB Kookmin card data on 119,000, Yegaram ~40,000.

incidents.sum: The lending software provider took Sageworks offline after detecting irregular activity, then confirmed a data security incident with unauthorised access. Sageworks holds the documents behind commercial and small-business loans, including borrowers' tax returns and financial statements. Abrigo serves more than 2,400 banks and credit unions.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Access contained. Whether borrower data was taken is unknown. Banks should review API logs and access scopes and check the 36-hour regulator notification rule.

incidents.t: Storm ransomware: five US banks and a credit union
incidents.sum: The Storm group listed five US banks with about $6.1bn in combined assets, plus Insight Credit Union. Sawyer Savings Bank and Insight have confirmed breaches; the other four have not commented. Sawyer notified 16,069 people that names and Social Security numbers were taken.
incidents.how: Sawyer's breach happened at the firm that runs its IT. The firm is not named.
tl: Sawyer closes its branches for a week.
incidents.fix: Two breaches confirmed, four unconfirmed.

incidents.t: European bank entered through a vendor gateway
incidents.sum: Unit 42 described an unnamed European bank where an attacker signed in with stolen credentials through a third-party-managed gateway, scanned thousands of systems, guessed administrator passwords, scraped internal documentation and tried to exploit the bank's WSUS update server.
incidents.how: Compromised credentials on an external gateway run by a vendor, where strict authentication was not enforced.
incidents.fix: Stopped before persistence. Credentials rotated and monitoring expanded.

incidents.t: State Bank of India records on the dark web
incidents.sum: India's largest bank disclosed a suspected cyberattack after customer records appeared on the dark web. Of about 375,000 records reviewed, nearly 4,000 held personal data: names, mobile numbers, birth dates, addresses and loan details.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Investigation open. The bank reports no material effect on operations.

incidents.t: AU Small Finance Bank data claim
incidents.sum: ScarlettGroup claims about 2.85 million records leaked from a third-party SaaS platform used by the bank.
incidents.how: Leak from a third-party platform.
incidents.fix: The bank says its own systems were unaffected.

incidents.t: SMBC Consumer Finance loan guarantee system
incidents.sum: Unauthorised access to the card-loan guarantee system exposed up to 320,118 people, including licence numbers, incomes and loan amounts.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Investigation open.

incidents.sum: Several Bank Rakyat pages, including the iRakyat online banking login, were defaced across multiple domains. A group calling itself MARLANWG claimed it.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: No data compromise disclosed. The bank has not confirmed an intrusion.

incidents.t: Indonesian banks: 1.2m attacks in a day
incidents.sum: Fortinet's FortiGuard Labs recorded more than 1.2 million attacks on Indonesian banking, finance and insurance in 24 hours, after 657,000 over the weekend. CIMB Niaga said it was monitoring and patching.
incidents.how: Attack type not specified.
tl: Regulator OJK starts liaising with banks.
OJK orders scrutiny and pausing of anomalous large transactions.
incidents.fix: No confirmed breaches or losses reported.

incidents.sum: The largest publicly reported crypto theft to date. Attackers reached the service that authorises wallet transactions and moved funds across ten blockchains. No private keys leaked; the legitimate signing system was made to sign.
incidents.how: An engineer installed a tampered Homebrew package after searching for an AI coding tool. A second sat fake job interviews and ran a malicious take-home task. On 20 October the attackers used Binance's internal AI tool to take over two more engineers.
tl: Fake interviews compromise a second engineer.
Draining starts 20:05 UTC, mostly done in 20 minutes.
FBI attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor.
US moves to seize $1.2bn of the stolen funds.
incidents.fix: US seizing $1.2bn; $2.7bn+ frozen in total. Binance set aside $6.34bn to cover users.

incidents.sum: One stolen application credential opened Microsoft 365 at hundreds of organisations. The backup service held standing consent to read customer tenants, so the attacker signed in as a trusted app with no password and no MFA prompt.
incidents.how: Abuse of the app credential. Microsoft tied it to Storm-0940, a China-aligned group using the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework.
tl: Backups available again through a new app.
incidents.fix: Contained 19 Oct. More than 300 successful tenant sign-ins seen by Huntress.

incidents.sum: Mass takeover of FortiGate firewalls and VPN gateways using valid logins, with access passed to ransomware affiliates. 86,644 working device credentials were verified.
incidents.how: Reused leaked credentials, brute force against devices without MFA, and cracked older password hashes.
incidents.fix: Ongoing.

incidents.sum: Attackers forced supermarket refrigeration controllers into overnight defrost cycles, spoiling stock at around 700 French sites and starting at least 15 fires. A second wave in early November hit thousands of units in at least 12 European countries, including a French blood bank.
incidents.how: Remote access to internet-exposed, often end-of-life controllers. French authorities attribute the first wave to Iran's Shahid Kaveh unit.
incidents.fix: Not closed. Agencies urge taking affected units offline.

incidents.sum: Four developer platforms lost customer secrets in a month. Zeabur (321,810 accounts) is shutting down. Railway, Northflank and Trigger.dev all had stored environment variables taken, and some customers saw their AI API tokens abused.
incidents.how: Zeabur: internal credentials not rotated after an August incident. Others: not disclosed, with early findings pointing at AI provider keys as the goal.
incidents.fix: Customers of all four told to rotate every stored key.

incidents.sum: Malicious builds of a widely used AI gateway library collected cloud keys, AI API keys, SSH keys and browser passwords on every Python start.
incidents.how: A master key committed to a public repository in May was used in October to get a privileged GitHub token.
incidents.fix: Commit corrected. The key itself had not been revoked at the time of reporting.

incidents.sum: One operator pointed autonomous AI agents at more than 1,200 websites and got into more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, for about $5,000 in AI usage.
incidents.how: The open-source Cairn platform found and exploited weaknesses with little supervision.
incidents.fix: Deere and SharkNinja report containment. Cummins investigating.

incidents.t: South Korea: ex-pentester with an AI framework
incidents.sum: A former penetration tester allegedly breached more than 90 organisations, took about 8.2 million records and extorted 38 victims. About 60 breaches came in six weeks once he paired a coding agent with ARTEX.
incidents.how: AI-assisted exploitation of exposed weaknesses.
incidents.fix: Suspect in custody.

incidents.sum: Ransomware encrypted customer virtual machines at a SoftBank group cloud provider, disrupting 495 companies and local governments, and wiped snapshots on the same platform.
incidents.how: A flaw in open-source software behind the portal login, then admin rights over virtualisation.
incidents.fix: Recovery in progress. No ransom paid.

incidents.sum: The glucose monitor maker said targeted phone calls to staff led to access to internal documents. ShinyHunters had listed the company days earlier.
incidents.how: Voice phishing of employees.
incidents.fix: At least eight lawsuits filed within days.

incidents.sum: An attacker posed as someone an employee trusted, took their login, reached customer data on third-party platforms and pushed a hacked-by notification to app users. 138,828 customers in the earlier count.
incidents.how: Impersonation of a trusted contact.
incidents.fix: Disclosed.

incidents.sum: Attackers talked their way into third-party-hosted business apps in June. October filings put the scope at 8,179,772 people, nearly the whole patient base.
incidents.how: Social engineering into business applications.
incidents.fix: No medical device or clinical system touched.

incidents.sum: A court employee clicked a malicious link. IT contained it within two hours, but the attackers had already copied a backup with 30 years of court-debt records and more than 150,000 foster care reports. About 1.3 million people.
incidents.how: One click on a phishing link.
incidents.fix: Contained in two hours. Data already taken.

incidents.sum: The blockchain investigations firm said attackers reached internal systems using what it called offensive agentic techniques. Later reporting said all live customer tokens were lost, including those of banks and law enforcement.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Investigation open.

incidents.sum: Malicious JavaScript replaced a third-party monitoring script and redirected logged-in users' funds. About $2.7m taken from 726 wallets in an hour.
incidents.how: The monitoring vendor's DNS was changed through its registrar.
incidents.fix: Customers to be reimbursed.

incidents.sum: Stolen GitHub tokens created more than 13,500 malicious branches across 850 accounts. Workflows printed secrets into build logs, which the attackers downloaded before deleting the runs.
incidents.how: Stolen tokens, including in private repositories.
incidents.fix: Revoke tokens and rotate every secret the workflows could read.

incidents.sum: Private keys behind an intermediate certificate authority were mathematically trivial, so certificates signed with them could not be trusted.
incidents.how: A key generation failure, not an intrusion.
incidents.fix: Certificates blocked.

incidents.sum: CISA and the FBI warned of a SafePay campaign against at least 600 organisations. October also saw Osaka Metropolitan University shut about 500 servers and UNM Health Sciences lose surgery capacity.
incidents.how: Varies by victim.
incidents.fix: Ongoing.

incidents.sum: The grocery group took websites and apps offline across its US and European chains. Stores stayed open and no data theft was found.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: No restoration date published.

incidents.sum: Registries for .gh, .sl and .as were breached. Attackers changed DNS for domains including Google's local addresses and got fraudulent certificates issued.
incidents.how: Registry systems compromised.
incidents.fix: Records restored, certificates revoked.

incidents.sum: Stolen management keys for a WordPress service were used to install backdoors and admin accounts on about 400,000 sites.
incidents.how: Theft of central keys from the vendor.
incidents.fix: Site owners told to remove unknown admins and reissue keys.

incidents.sum: Commercial spyware reached at least 45 devices through malicious ads that needed no click.
incidents.how: Zero-click delivery through ad content.
incidents.fix: Not disclosed.

incidents.t: Equinor: ongoing attack on IT systems
incidents.sum: Europe's largest gas supplier said it had detected an ongoing cyberattack on some of its IT systems. It says oil and gas production is not affected and it has found no sign of data theft.
incidents.how: Not disclosed. Equinor has not said how the attackers got in, whether ransomware is involved, or which systems were hit.
tl: Equinor statement at 18:55 CET. Authorities informed.
Update: attack still ongoing, production normal.
incidents.fix: Ongoing. No timetable for resolution.

incidents.t: Infoblox via a SharePoint migration vendor
incidents.sum: The DNS and network security company confirmed that attackers reached company data through a compromised data migration vendor. Reporting says the stolen material includes configuration snapshots of some customers' NIOS deployments and employee personal data, including Social Security numbers and direct deposit details.
incidents.how: The vendor had trusted access to Infoblox's SharePoint. Attackers used the vendor's accounts to pull data straight out of SharePoint.
incidents.fix: Investigation ongoing. Infoblox says no products, cloud services or software updates were involved. Customers using NIOS should ask whether their snapshots were taken and rotate any secrets inside them.

incidents.t: Osaki Electric: ransomware halts smart-meter production
incidents.sum: The Japanese smart-meter maker found encrypted data on its servers and disconnected its external networks. Production was still stopped on 19 November. The company did not report that meters already installed were affected.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Restart date unknown. Data leak under investigation.

incidents.t: NVIDIA listed by the Gentlemen ransomware group
incidents.sum: The Gentlemen group added NVIDIA to its leak site with a countdown ending on 28 November, without publishing proof. NVIDIA says it has found no evidence its own systems were compromised and is looking into a separate incident that may have affected one of its service providers.
incidents.how: Unknown. NVIDIA points to a possible incident at a service provider.
incidents.fix: Claim not verified.

incidents.t: Quantum Systems drones grounded after attack
incidents.sum: The German drone maker confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted its operations, and the German military grounded the company's drones. Reports point to a malicious software update.
incidents.how: Reported as a malicious software update; not confirmed by the company.
tl: Attack confirmed; military grounds the drones.
incidents.fix: Under investigation.

incidents.sum: The Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital in Thuringia reopened its emergency room after an extortion attack. Investigators are working on the case and no state link has emerged.
incidents.how: Not disclosed.
incidents.fix: Investigation open.

incidents.sum: The backend of the Paytaca Bitcoin Cash wallet was exploited, enabling fraudulent peer-to-peer orders and unauthorised payment requests.
incidents.how: Backend exploitation; method not stated.
incidents.fix: Remediation not stated.

incidents.sum: An unsafe deserialization flaw in the blog server's XML-RPC endpoint lets an attacker run code with no login, in every release from 4.0.0 to 6.1.4. Apache says it is being actively exploited. It is the same bug as CVE-2026-82384, which had listed only 6.1.5.
incidents.how: A crafted request to /roller-services/xmlrpc, reachable even when XML-RPC is switched off in the admin screen. A proof of concept has been public since 28 September.
tl: Apache widens it to 4.0.0–6.1.4 and confirms exploitation.
incidents.fix: Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later (6.1.7 recommended) or block the XML-RPC endpoint. Not yet on CISA's exploited list at the time of writing.

incidents.sum: Any machine holding a signed agent certificate can run code on the Puppet Server, the system that pushes configuration to every managed machine. Where the certificate authority auto-signs requests, an attacker with no credentials can get such a certificate. A working exploit is public.
incidents.how: A crafted report sent to the server is deserialized unsafely.
tl: Disclosed by Perforce, Vox Pupuli and Neodyme.
CISA adds it to its exploited list.
CISA deadline for US federal agencies.
incidents.fix: Fixed in Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1, and patched OpenVox releases. Turn off certificate auto-signing.

watch.sum: Five memory-safety flaws in nginx and NGINX Plus, disclosed by Xint and fixed by F5 on 18 November. Each can crash a worker process and can lead to remote code execution with no login where ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed. The most exposed one, CVE-2026-123007, sits in HTTP/2 flow control and is in every release since HTTP/2 arrived in 1.9.5 (2015). Xint chains it with a separate, still unpatched Linux kernel SCTP flaw to reach root. No exploitation or EPSS score reported as of 19 November.

watch.act: Upgrade to nginx 1.30.7 (stable) or 1.31.9 (mainline), then restart. Linux distributions backport fixes under older version numbers, so check your distribution's advisory rather than nginx -v alone. Where patching must wait, turning off HTTP/2 closes two of the five. Check appliances and containers that bundle nginx.

watch.sum: A memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder can give remote code execution with no login in Jenkins, Jira, Keycloak and other Java products under some configurations. notAttacks.t: Not cyberattacks: the 12–17 November outage wave
notAttacks.sum: Microsoft 365 (from 12 Nov), the FAA ground stop (13 Nov), JPMorgan Chase and other US banks (16 Nov), Apple services and NSANet (17 Nov) all went down within a few days. Each organisation gave a technical or maintenance cause. On 18 November the DHS Secretary, the Director of National Intelligence and the FBI Deputy Director told a House committee the outages were not malicious.

2026-10.head: October: AI-driven intrusion goes mainstream, and vendors become the shortest route in.
pts: The largest crypto theft on record (Binance, $6.3bn) began with a fake job interview and a tampered developer tool.
ARTEX and Cairn showed one operator with AI agents can breach dozens of organisations in weeks.
Edge devices (Ivanti, BeyondTrust, Cisco) were exploited before or within days of a fix.

2026-11.head: November so far: suppliers and stolen access, with banks squarely in range.
pts: Arkéa, Visa, Mastercard, Infoblox, Expedia and TSMC were all reached through a third party.
Email remained the front door: an exploited Outlook flaw and two exploited Barracuda gateway flaws.
Energy and industry joined the list in the last week: Equinor, Osaki Electric and Quantum Systems.
Two critical patch waves landed on 17–18 November without known exploitation yet: Java4Shell and nginx2root. Internet-facing nginx with HTTP/2 is the widest exposure.
A wave of outages was not an attack; keep rumours out of incident counts.
